Keyboard and accessible play in Beacon Lattice

A source-checked overview of Beacon Lattice’s native buttons, coordinate selectors, cell labels, and keyboard limits—not an accessibility certification.

By NoCharge·Reviewed by NoCharge·Published August 19, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

Cover every cell. Overlap nothing.

Play Beacon LatticeBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: Current Beacon Lattice uses buttons and standard row-and-column selectors for its five-piece exact-cover puzzle. Its documented keyboard path is based on those controls, not on old arrow-key or number-key shortcuts.

Choose and place a piece

Use Tab or Shift+Tab to move through the inventory buttons, Rotate beacon, Undo placement, the anchor row and column selectors, the placement button, and the board buttons. Enter or Space activates a focused button; the selectors use the browser’s native selection behavior. An uncovered board button can also be activated to use that square as the anchor.

The puzzle contains five distinct pentominoes—F, V, I, U, and L—on an empty five-by-five board. Choose a shape, rotate it, set an anchor, and place it only if all five cells fit without overlap.

What the board names

Board buttons include their row and column and whether the square is uncovered or covered by a numbered beacon. The live status message describes a successful placement, an invalid fit, an undo, or a completed puzzle. The visible number on a covered square identifies its piece; it is not a 0/1/2+ coverage total.

Limits to keep clear

The current UI does not expose arrow-key grid movement, number-key shape selection, locked starting beacons, or stored best results. Native controls provide a keyboard route through the visible actions, but that description is not a certification and does not establish compatibility with every browser, screen reader, or input setup. Test the live page with the tools and settings you use.

Reset returns the board and five-piece inventory to the same starting state. For the exact placement goal, see How exact coverage works in Beacon Lattice.
